findings.title: Fabricated runtime dependency `typing-extensions>=4.0.0` is never used and breaks network-less installation
findings.detail: /workspace/pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = ["typing-extensions>=4.0.0"]`. findings.title: _levenshtein_norm('', '') raises ZeroDivisionError rather than returning a value in 0..1 (upstream-identical)
findings.detail: Spec entry 1 describes `_levenshtein_norm(source, target) -> float` as a "normalized (0..1) Levenshtein distance, divided by max string length". When both arguments are empty the divisor `max(len(source), len(target))` is 0, so the function raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning a float. This is NOT a workspace defect: all four authoritative reference copies on disk (the spec-matching 89c78413 snapshot, the fab01f5f snapshot, /tmp/repo/docopt-ng-0.9.0 and /tmp/src/docopt_ng-0.9.0) behave byte-identically, and per the audit rules upstream is the authority. It is also unreachable through the public `docopt()` entry point: the only caller is `_parse_longer`, which compares `longer` (always starts with '--', so len >= 2) against `o.longer` filtered by a truthiness guard, so neither operand can be empty. Reported as info so the discrepancy between spec prose and real behaviour is on the record.
findings.suggested_fix: No change. Modifying /workspace would diverge from upstream, which the audit rules make authoritative. If the specification prose is ever revised, entry 1 could note that the normalization is undefined when both inputs are empty.
